name: Thriveworks
one_liner: In-person or video therapy and psychiatry with Thriveworks clinicians, billed to insurance (incl. Medicare) or self-pay per session.

People who want the choice of in-person or online sessions

short_description: National therapy and psychiatry practice with in-person and online sessions; in network with 360+ insurance plans, or $200 first session and $170.
long_description: Thriveworks is a US mental health practice with more than 2,000 clinicians offering individual, child and teen, couples and family therapy, plus psychiatry and medication management where available by state. You can choose in-person or online sessions, and the company says most people start within a week. Its pricing page lists 360+ insurance plans, including UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, Cigna, BCBS, Humana, Anthem, Tricare and Medicare (though some provider types, such as LPCs and MFTs, cannot take Medicare); Medicaid is not accepted. Copays typically run $0–$55. Self-pay therapy is $200 for the first session and $170 after in most states, higher in some (for example $240 and $195 in Massachusetts); psychiatry is $300 first visit and $210 follow-ups in most states. There is no membership fee. Its privacy policy says it does not sell data for money but shares identifiers and browsing data with Meta and Google for cross-context advertising if you accept marketing cookies.
patient_summary: You find a Thriveworks therapist or psychiatric provider by location, book online or by phone, and meet in person or by video, usually within a week. Most people pay an insurance copay (typically $0–$55); self-pay therapy is about $170–$200 a session. Medicaid is not accepted.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance (typically $0–$55); $200 first session, then $170/session self-pay in most states
pricing.notes: Self-pay varies by state (e.g. $240 then $195 in Massachusetts). Psychiatry self-pay $300 first visit, $210 follow-up in most states. 360+ plans including Medicare; Medicaid not accepted. No membership fee.

privacy.notes: Clinical records are under a HIPAA notice, but the website shares identifiers and browsing data with Meta and Google for advertising if you accept marketing cookies; deletion rights are listed only for some states and the EU.

seo.meta_description: Thriveworks offers in-person and video therapy with licensed counselors across 40+ states, accepting most major insurance plans.

faqs.a: Thriveworks accepts most major insurance including Aetna, Cigna, BCBS, UnitedHealthcare, Humana, Tricare, and Medicare. Coverage varies by location. Enter your insurance on their website to verify coverage and find in-network providers near you.

Yes, Thriveworks has 340+ physical locations across 40+ states offering in-person therapy. You can also choose video sessions. Many clients alternate between in-person and video depending on their schedule. Check location availability in your area.

faqs.q: How much does Thriveworks cost without insurance?
faqs.a: Self-pay rates are $99-200 per session depending on provider type (therapist vs psychologist vs psychiatrist) and location. Sliding scale may be available. With insurance, you pay your standard copay, typically $20-50.

faqs.q: How is Thriveworks different from BetterHelp?
faqs.a: Thriveworks offers both in-person and video therapy with insurance billing, while BetterHelp is online-only with subscription pricing. If you have insurance and want in-person options, Thriveworks is often more affordable. BetterHelp is simpler for those preferring text-based support.
